Do Laws Requiring People to Report Crimes Violate the First Amendment?

It seems to me that, for all the reasons he gives and based on the reasoning of the 2d Circuit’s holding, the arguments for such laws being a violation of the Constitutional are much stronger than the arguments in favor of such laws. I don’t see why he is struggling with the issue of First Amendment applicability to government compelled speech generally at the end.

Since each instance of compelled speech is for a different government end (collection of taxes, completion of the Constitutionally required census, etc), each requires its own test and each may have a different answer. There’s no real need to answer a question before it is a case or controversy being adjudicated by the courts. And the strict scrutiny test will still be the same. The ends may be more or less compelling and the less burdensome alternatives will differ. So some other laws may be fine and some may be unConstitutional. At the end of the day each will need to be litigated separately. Even with as objective and clear a standard as possible, it will still end up being a judgment call for each different category.
